name: Phenylephrine
executiveSummary: Pure α1 vasopressor. Adult: bolus **50–200 µg IV**; infusion **0.1–1.5 µg/kg/min** or **20–200 µg/min**. Pediatrics: bolus **1–5 µg/kg**; infusion **0.1–0.5 µg/kg/min**. Reflex bradycardia common.
indications:
## Indications

- Perioperative hypotension / vasodilation (spinal anesthesia, etc.).
- Vasodilatory shock adjunct when profile (high HR, low SVR) favors it.
- Anaphylaxis regimens only if institutional protocol includes it (epinephrine remains first-line).

## Precautions

- **Reflex bradycardia**; caution in ischemic heart disease, baseline bradycardia, severe HTN.
- Extravasation → necrosis; prefer central line for continuous infusion.
- Does not replace volume.

> Titrate to BP goal with adequate monitoring.

adulto.dose: Bolus: **50–100 µg** IV (repeat; some use up to **200 µg**). Infusion: **0.1–0.5 µg/kg/min** (wide range **0.1–1.5 µg/kg/min**) or fixed **20–200 µg/min** per card.
adulto.administration: Dilute in NS/D5W (e.g. 10 mg in 100 mL = 100 µg/mL). Slow bolus; pump infusion.
adulto.notes: Institutional ready push-dose: follow exact card.

pediatrico.dose: Bolus **1–5 µg/kg**. Infusion **0.1–0.5 µg/kg/min** (titrate; institutional ceilings vary).
pediatrico.administration: IV on pump; central preferred for continuous.

neonatal.dose: Only per NNU card (bolus/infusion in µg/kg).

stability:
## Stability

- Use fresh dilution or per product label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Reflex bradycardia, hypertension, headache, anxiety, extravasation/peripheral ischemia.
